fluff.overview: The MRM Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle mounting three MRM-30 launchers on the standard carrier chassis. Developed by the Quikscell Company as a variant of the SRM/LRM Carrier family, the MRM Carrier emerged during the FedCom Civil War era to exploit medium-range missile technology. A C3 slave unit enables networked targeting to compensate for the MRM system's inherent inaccuracy at extended range.
fluff.capabilities:
The MRM Carrier mounts three MRM-30 launchers as its primary armament, supplemented by a C3 slave unit for networked targeting data. An InterComBust 180 internal combustion engine maintains the standard fifty-four kilometer per hour top speed. Lexington Ltd. High Grade ferro-fibrous armor provides fifty-three points of protection, improved over the standard carrier's Simple Armor Plate.

A Communicator system with C3 link and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting enable coordination with C3 master units. Each MRM-30 launcher carries only eight rounds, giving the vehicle limited endurance before requiring resupply. The MRM system's inherent scatter pattern makes it most effective against clustered targets or in area-denial roles.
fluff.deployment: Quikscell produced the MRM Carrier at its Oliver facility beginning around 3063. The design found modest adoption across the Inner Sphere, often paired with ECM-equipped units to protect the slow-moving carrier from electronic countermeasures during engagements.
fluff.history:
The MRM Carrier was introduced by Quikscell as a variant during the FedCom Civil War era, mounting three MRM-30 launchers with a C3 slave unit on the standard carrier chassis. TRO:3058 Upgrade describes it as 'almost an entirely new design,' noting that it is often paired with ECM-equipped units as it is too slow to keep up in swift advances. Each launcher carries only eight rounds, requiring frequent resupply.

Quikscell produced the MRM Carrier at its Oliver facility for distribution across the Inner Sphere. The design found modest popularity as a middle-ground between the long-range LRM Carrier and the close-range SRM Carrier, though limited ammunition capacity remained a persistent complaint.
